title: Ryan Neelam Steps Up to Lead Australia-India Ties
excerpt: The seasoned diplomat takes the helm of CAIR as Canberra and New Delhi double down on like-minded partnerships amid global disorder.
body:
Ryan Neelam, a veteran Australian diplomat and foreign policy researcher, has taken charge as Chief Executive Officer of the Centre for Australia-India Relations (CAIR), stepping into the role at a moment when both nations are actively deepening their ties with democratic partners to hedge against a turbulent global order.

**Who is Ryan Neelam:**
Neelam brings formidable credentials to the job. He served for 14 years as an Australian diplomat, including as acting Consul-General to Hong Kong and Macau, and as a representative at the Australian Mission to the United Nations in New York, where he helped negotiate the UN Sustainable Development Goals and worked on Australia's term on the UN Security Council. Most recently, he led the Public Opinion and Foreign Policy Program at the Lowy Institute, overseeing its flagship annual poll and the Global Diplomacy Index.

**Why this moment matters:**
Neelam assumes leadership of CAIR as both Australia and India publicly prioritise 'like-minded' democratic partners over great-power dependence. India has signed a Declaration on Security Cooperation with Japan, welcomed Australia's first defence trade mission, and is pursuing an EU-India Security and Defence Partnership — all against the backdrop of geopolitical uncertainty driven by shifting US foreign policy. Australia, for its part, has deepened its Comprehensive Strategic Partnership with India and held an inaugural Defence Ministers' Dialogue in October 2025. The Centre itself, launched by Prime Minister Albanese in 2023, serves as a national platform strengthening collaboration between both countries across government, industry, academia and civil society.

**What to watch:**
With Prime Minister Modi's visit to Australia expected in July 2026, Neelam's early priorities at CAIR — and his ability to translate diplomatic momentum into tangible outcomes — will face an important early test.
